title: Name the operator-questions skill and diagram mod in README and runbook
description: README.md and docs/runbooks/install-and-switch-an-output-style.md name the operator-questions skill and the diagram mod, and the runtime the helper needs (bun or node on PATH), per the design in opum-doc docs/reference/operator-questions-skill-design.md at opum-doc origin/main 1312f0c, section Changes this needs in plain-english-styles item 7.

acceptanceCriteria.text: README.md names the operator-questions skill and the diagram mod
docs/runbooks/install-and-switch-an-output-style.md names the skill and the mod
Both name the runtime the helper needs: bun or node on PATH

finalSummary:
README and runbook now name the operator-questions skill and the diagram mod, and the runtime the helper needs. README gains an "Operator questions and diagrams" section: what the skill does, what the mod draws (Unicode art on the terminal, SVG on desktop, VS Code and mobile, with the Open diagram fallback), and that the mod runs its helper with bun or node on PATH, keeping the source and saying so when neither is found. The runbook gains "The skill and the diagram mod" with the same facts at install depth, plus the runtime note.

The runbook also records the residual limit the leader flagged, as a known limit of the DEFAULT checks: code_block_size exempts a mermaid fence only when it opens with a Mermaid diagram type, and the two checks that close the rest of the gap (diagram_parses and diagram_size) are opt-in per case, named by the decision cases. So in an ordinary reply a fence tagged mermaid whose first line is flowchart TD and whose body is prose still leaves the word budget. Stated as a limit of the default checks, not as a closed gap.

lore sync ran and added two entries to docs/log.md, the managed block. Gates: lore check exit 0 (24 files, 0 errors); npm --prefix harness test 262 pass / 0 fail; claude plugin test 21/21; claude plugin validate exit 0; node src/cli.mjs audit exit 0, all 12 checks agree.
